paper.title: When More Objectives Make Identification Easier: The Role of Preferences and Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Fixed-confidence multi-objective best-arm identification (Gaussian vector feedback, preference-induced answer map)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Multi-objective (vector-valued) rewards are out of scope per ontology scope rules.
unmapped: each arm has an M-dimensional mean vector; each pull reveals the full reward vector with N(0, I_M) noise
answer is the set of maximal arms under a known preference order (Pareto, linear scalarization, lexicographic) or any finite-range answer map
the learner knows the preference relation and a model class Theta of feasible instances (e.g. common-ranking restriction)
local stability of the true instance (answer unchanged in a Frobenius ball)
settings.definition_quote: We consider a stochastic multi-armed bandit with $K\ge2$ arms and $M\ge1$ objectives... observes $X_t=\mu_{I_t}+\varepsilon_t, \varepsilon_t\sim\mathcal N(0,I_M)$... For an instance $\bmu$, the prescribed answer is the complete set of maximal arms

symbols.T_pref: characteristic time T_preceq(mu) = 1/sup_w inf_{nu in Alt} (1/2) sum_i w_i ||mu_i - nu_i||^2

conditions: any algorithm that is delta-correct on Theta

source.label: thm:lower-bound
source.quote: For any $\delta\in(0,1/2)$, any algorithm that is $\delta$-correct on $\Theta$, and any $\bmu\in\Theta$, $\E_{\bmu}[\tau_\delta] \ge T_{\preceq}(\bmu)\kl(1-\delta,\delta) \Rightarrow \liminf_{\delta\downarrow0} \frac{\E_{\bmu}[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)} \ge T_{\preceq}(\bmu)$

results.notes: Finite-delta form of the unified characteristic-time lower bound.

conditions: any algorithm that is delta-correct on Theta
every instance in Theta satisfies local stability (Assumption 1) and has a nonempty alternative set
tuning: stopping threshold beta(t,delta) = KM/2 + sqrt(KM log(2(t+1)^{K+2}/delta)) + log(2(t+1)^{K+2}/delta)

source.label: thm:optimality
source.quote: Suppose every instance in $\Theta$ satisfies Assumption~\ref{ass:local-stability} and has a nonempty alternative set. Then \textnormal{OATS} is $\delta$-correct, and for every $\bmu\in\Theta$, $\lim_{\delta\downarrow0} \frac{\E_{\bmu}[\tau_\delta]}{\log(1/\delta)} = T_{\preceq}(\bmu)$.

results.notes: Paper states an exact limit; recorded as upper (limsup) side; matching lower side is Theorem 1. OATS is delta-correct. Computation requires solving inf over alternatives; not stated polynomial. Propositions 1-4 and Lemma 1 compute characteristic times for two-arm instances (e.g. T_P = 16/(M Delta^2), T_lex=8/Delta^2) and are not recorded as separate guarantees.
